title: RAMageddon is ready to rage on through 2030
snippet: SK Hynix, one of the major companies behind memory production, says that it’s sold out through 2029, leaving RAMageddon ready to rage on for at least the next three years. more…
fullText:
SK Hynix, one of the major companies behind memory production, says that it’s sold out through 2029, leaving RAMageddon ready to rage on for at least the next three years.

On its latest earnings call today, SK Hynix confirmed that production of both DRAM and HBM (high-bandwidth memory) are effectively sold out not just for this year, not just for next year, but through 2029. That puts RAMageddon, the global shortage of memory, lasting at least another three years before we see any relief.

SK Hynix’s CFO explains (via The Motley Fool, Seeking Alpha):

…memory supply cannot keep pace with this level of demand growth, thus, we expect it to be difficult to fully meet customers’ volume requirements in the near term, given the complexities involved in implementing leading-edge processes and the lead times required to construct new production facilities. A situation where supply cannot keep up with demand is expected to persist for some time, a constraint projected to continue through 2030.

Micron, one of the other companies responsible for memory production, previously said to expect 2027 to be “even tighter” compared to 2026. 

	

The SK Hynix call also details how the company is making long-term agreements which already account for “more than 50% of our total capacity for 2027 and 2028.”

SK Hynix isn’t the biggest name in DRAM/HBM production, with Samsung accounting for a larger share, but everyone else is dealing with the same constraints. PCMag points out that SK Hynix is working to build out more production capacity, as everyone else is too, but it takes time to build out the complex infrastructure.

Buckle up folks, this isn’t ending anytime soon. 🫠

title: Major Even Realities G2 smart glasses update adds Conversate ‘Pro Mode,’ Knowledge Base
snippet: Even Realities today announced that a new software version will be rolling out to the G2 smart glasses, complete with a personal knowledge base that, thankfully, only remembers what you tell it. more…
fullText:
Even Realities today announced that a new software version will be rolling out to the G2 smart glasses, complete with a personal knowledge base that, thankfully, only remembers what you tell it.

When the G2 smart glasses launched, Even Realities packed them with features aimed at professionals, as well as tech geeks who appreciate retro mixing with the modern. But features like Conversate can be valuable to anyone in the right situation.

Even Realities says Conversate is getting an overhauled “Pro Mode” that pulls data from something it’s calling Knowledge Base – a feature that remembers the information and data you select. These feature refreshes are included in the Even Realities G2 version 2.4.0 update, which also upgrades the company’s AI interface to Even AI 2.0.

In order, it works like this:

	

Files and audio recorded in Conversate mode on the Even Realities G2 glasses, along with any manually uploaded files, sync to a secure Google Cloud Platform server in the EU.

Knowledge Base updates your information to disseminate.

Even AI 2.0 and active Conversate sessions pull context from the Knowledge Base.

Even Realities allows users to select up to 10 Conversate records to upload to that context tree during the initial setup. More can be added as they’re recorded. It also seems that new Conversate sessions need to be selected for upload and won’t be added to that database automatically, unless the user toggles automated uploads on.

Whatever data is there, Conversate Pro Mode will surface during relevant sessions. For instance, if you’re a sports journalist and have a backlog of recorded meetings in Conversate, new instances will provide context based on what you already know. It’s a more trustworthy approach than letting an AI model surface information it thinks is relevant. Even AI won’t stop doing that, but the Knowledge Base might be a more palatable source for some.

The biggest part of this update comes down to Even AI 2.0. Even Realities says it’s a “major upgrade” to how users interact with the G2 glasses as a whole. In reality, it comes down to quality-of-life changes that should make the smart glasses easier to use.

The G2 glasses are now able to activate Even AI with the touch sensor. When you hold it down, the recording starts, but stops when you release. And instead of requiring a new wake word for a follow-up, users can enable multi-turn conversations. Opening Even Hubs apps and changing certain settings right from the AI chat are supported, too.

Even Realities says Knowledge Base and Conversate Pro Mode will both launch today in beta. Because it’s still an early feature, it will be limited for users based on a monthly usage allowance. There’s no mention of pricing after beta in Even Realities’ press release.

Oh, and there’s a new tortoiseshell color option.

snippet: iPadOS 27.2 arrived this week as the latest noteworthy iPad software update, here are two new features it includes. more…
fullText:
iPadOS 27.2 arrived this week as the latest noteworthy iPad software update, here are two new features it includes.

#1: Siri AI contextual popup and more improvements

Siri AI is a major improvement over the old Siri, and I’m using it all the time on my iPad—often with a CMD + Space keyboard shortcut since Siri and Spotlight are now integrated.

In iPadOS 27.2, Apple added another convenient way to interact with Siri that first debuted on the Mac in macOS Golden Gate.

When you select text in iPadOS 27.2 via a trackpad or mouse, there’s a new Siri contextual popup that appears to the left of your selection. If you hover over the Siri icon with your cursor, it instantly expands to offer an ‘Ask Siri’ text field.

This makes it quick and easy to ask Siri about whatever you’ve highlighted. And if you’re in the writing process, the Siri popup even has suggestions like ‘Proofread,’ ‘Rewrite,’ and ‘How does this sound?’ so you can get help with just a click.

Siri AI also includes several new upgrades that make it more capable. Per Apple’s release notes:

Siri AI can recall your past conversations, so you can ask Siri about something it told you before, like the restaurants it recommended last week

Siri AI can draw from more sources to give you a great answer, including photos attached in Messages, Calendar event attendees, your voicemails, and better results from Safari history and Reading List

#2: Profiles in Apple TV app

iPads make great video devices whether you’re an adult or a kid. And if you share an iPad with a partner or child, the Apple TV app has a welcome new addition: user profiles.

iPadOS 27.2 brings over the same profiles feature that tvOS already offered on Apple TV 4K.

When you open the Apple TV app on iPad, you’ll see a new profile selection screen at startup. From here, you can choose who’s watching and the TV app will automatically update its queue, playback history, and content recommendations based on your selection.

If you’re a parent, profiles will take content restrictions into account. So when your child’s profile is active, they’ll only see films and TV shows that match the age settings you’ve previously set.

And if you don’t want to use profiles, it’s easy to disable them from showing on startup with a quick tap.

fullText:

title: Google Home and Nest speakers getting seven updates, including for Bluetooth & audio quality
snippet: In addition to Chromecast with Google TV and Nest Wifi Pro updates, Google detailed what new firmware for Nest and Home speakers brings. more…
fullText:
In addition to Chromecast with Google TV and Nest Wifi Pro updates, Google detailed what new firmware for Nest and Home speakers brings.

The Google Home, Google Home Mini, and Nest Audio benefit from “enhanced streaming performance” that should result in “smoother audio playback.”

There’s also “faster and more reliable local device discovery” in the Google Home app for the Google Home Speaker, Nest Audio, and Nest Mini.

On the audio front, be on the lookout for:

	

Speaker Pair Volume Tuning: Improved audio quality by reducing boomy bass and ensuring minimum volume levels remain clearly audible.

Bluetooth Audio Streaming on Resume: Fixed a bug where Bluetooth audio streaming from a connected laptop or device would automatically pause after receiving a voice “resume” command.

Speaker Group & Stereo Pair Visibility: Fixed an issue where stereo pairs and speaker groups could unexpectedly disappear or become undiscoverable in the Google Home app.

Google has resolved an issue that prevented smart speakers from “connecting to Wi-Fi 7 access points using WPA3 security.”

The final update addresses an issue “where users were unable to end Google Meet calls using voice commands.”

Google did not specify the firmware versions for these updates, and its release notes page has not been fully updated yet (e.g., Google Home Speaker).

The full changelog is below:

Audio playback: Enhanced streaming performance on Nest Audio, Google Home, and Google Home Mini for smoother audio playback. 

Speaker Pair Volume Tuning: Improved audio quality by reducing boomy bass and ensuring minimum volume levels remain clearly audible.

Local Network Discovery: Improved faster and more reliable local device discovery within the Google Home app for Google Home Speaker, Google Nest Audio, and Google Nest Mini.

Bluetooth Audio Streaming on Resume: Fixed a bug where Bluetooth audio streaming from a connected laptop or device would automatically pause after receiving a voice “resume” command.

Wi-Fi 7 Router Compatibility: Resolved setup and connection failures preventing smart speakers from connecting to Wi-Fi 7 access points using WPA3 security.

Speaker Group & Stereo Pair Visibility: Fixed an issue where stereo pairs and speaker groups could unexpectedly disappear or become undiscoverable in the Google Home app.

Google Meet Voice Call Controls: Fixed an issue where users were unable to end Google Meet calls using voice commands

title: iOS 27.3 release date: Here’s when to expect new iPhone features
snippet: Apple released iOS 27.2 this week with new features for Messages, Siri AI, and Photos, plus an Apple Music rebrand and more. But work on iOS 27.3 is already well underway, here’s when to expect the next big iPhone update. more…
fullText:
Apple released iOS 27.2 this week with new features for Messages, Siri AI, and Photos, plus an Apple Music rebrand and more. But work on iOS 27.3 is already well underway, here’s when to expect the next big iPhone update.

iOS 27.3 is almost available in beta, with public launch expected in mid-December

If you follow Apple closely, the company’s software release patterns quickly become clear.

For example, iOS 27.2 launched this week right around the same time as Apple’s previous releases in years past.

The only difference is that normally we would have expected iOS 27.1 in the last week of October rather than 27.2. But due to Apple making iOS 27.1 exclusive to iPhone Duo, all software releases for the iOS 27 cycle will be off by one number—despite following the same timing as ever.

That means iOS 27.3 is up next, and its release should align with historic patterns for x.2 updates.

iOS 27.3 is expected to arrive in beta within the next few days—Monday, November 2 is likely.

As for the public launch, here’s what past years have shown for comparable x.2 updates:

iOS 26.2: Friday, December 12

iOS 18.2: Wednesday, December 11

iOS 17.2: Monday, December 11

	

Based on this pattern, iOS 27.3 is expected to release in mid-December.

Apple always tries to ship its last software update of the year with a little buffer before taking a holiday break. That way if any major issues arise, the company can develop a quick fix and push it out before much of the company takes time off.

As for new iPhone features in iOS 27.3, we’ll know a lot more after the beta arrives. So far though, at a minimum we’re expecting the additional Siri AI languages Apple announced this week, plus the return of the all-new Health app.

Will you install the iOS 27.3 beta or wait for the release version? Let us know in the comments.

title: Andy Jassy says Prime Video is on track to earn ‘tens of billions of dollars’
snippet: The success of blockbuster hits like "Project Hail Mary" and "Verity" is only part of the story, Amazon's CEO says.
fullText:
It’s been four years since Amazon bought MGM for $8.5 billion. But coming off the blockbuster success of this year’s hit movie “Project Hail Mary,” Hollywood has become a lucrative business for the e-commerce giant.

Prime Video, Amazon’s streaming service, “has emerged as a significant business with a revenue run rate in the tens of billions of dollars and is now profitable in its own right,” Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said on the quarterly earnings call on Thursday. Jassy had previously told investors in May that Prime Video was profitable, but being on track to generate tens of billions is a new detail.

Amazon said its movie studio, Amazon MGM Studios, has brought in more than $1.2 billion in global box office sales so far this year, helped by hits like “Project Hail Mary” and “Verity.” 

“Project Hail Mary” grossed an estimated $684 million worldwide, according to The Numbers. Starring Ryan Gosling and based on Andy Weir’s novel, the film opened in theaters in March and became Amazon MGM Studios’ highest-grossing release, according to entertainment reports. (The studio also had at least one notable flop this year: “Melania.”)

Jassy also named a number of TV shows as hits, including “Carrie,” “The Summer I Turned Pretty,” “The Boys,” “Off Campus,” “Fallout,” and “Reacher.” Season 4 of “Reacher” drew 66 million viewers globally in its first 28 days, the company says, with more to come. Season 5 is filming now, and the show was picked up for a sixth season. (And if you don’t follow Alan Ritchson, the star of “Reacher,” on Threads, you are missing out on an actor who has turned a friendly-yet-witty reply into an art form.)

Sports have also been a significant driver. Prime Video broadcasts NASCAR, the Masters, and UEFA Champions League soccer, but Thursday Night Football appears to be its biggest success this year. The first six games of this season have averaged 17.7 million viewers, up 16% from last year, according to Nielsen figures Amazon shared. The streaming service also attracted over 2 million viewers for its second season of the NBA on Prime, Nielsen said.

Prime Video, Amazon’s streaming service, “has emerged as a significant business with a revenue run rate in the tens of billions of dollars and is now profitable in its own right,” Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said on the quarterly earnings call on Thursday. Jassy had previously told investors in May that Prime Video was profitable, but being on track to generate tens of billions is a new detail.

snippet: It’s time to upgrade my old Nest Thermostat to the latest 4th-gen model, and the bundle even includes a fancy new Nest Temperature Sensor (2nd gen), all for a new low price of $219! more…
fullText:
It’s time to upgrade my old Nest Thermostat to the latest 4th-gen model, and the bundle even includes a fancy new Nest Temperature Sensor (2nd gen), all for a new low price of $219!

Google’s most gorgeous thermostat is ready to get you saving money this winter, and I don’t just mean because of this great deal. If you have an older Nest thermostat or have been looking to upgrade to Nest this year, now’s the ideal time thanks to this $60-off Nest Thermostat 4th-gen deal.

Nest Thermostat 4th-gen deal at Amazon

This is the lowest price we’ve seen in a bit for the latest thermostat in Google’s lineup, nearly matching last year’s Black Friday low, and it also includes a Nest Temperature Sensor (2nd gen) that you can put somewhere else in your home to help the thermostat better regulate the temperature across your house. Ideally, this sensor would go in a room that’s always hotter or colder than the rest of the house (we all have one of those, right?).

Google launched the 4th-gen Nest Learning Thermostat in fall 2024 after a solid decade of no hardware updates to the “Learning Thermostat” line. My particular 3rd-gen Learning Thermostat came out way back in 2015, and while Google has been good about supporting it over the years, I imagine the clock is ticking for end-of-life support pretty soon. The first two generations lost support in 2025.

	

The new design is doggone gorgeous, with a very Pixel Watch-like design that comes in three fantastic colors: Silver, Gold, and Obsidian. All three colors are polished like they just came out of a jewelry store and look stunning even in the most boring hallway. Aside from its good looks, this one packs Google Home and Gemini smarts, a new Dynamic Farsight feature powered by Soli, the rotating bezel everyone loves, Smart Ventilation air quality measurement, and a ton of other great features in the Google Home app.

This model doesn’t require a C-wire to function, so it’s compatible with a ton of HVAC systems and includes an easy step-by-step guide within the Google Home app to get you started. Don’t worry, I have zero electrical wiring experience, and I got mine hooked up right the first time, so be sure to upgrade to this Nest Thermostat 4th-gen deal today and get to saving money with Gemini smarts this winter.

title: XREAL Aura debuts with 150 made-for-XR experiences, including Project Hail Mary, NBA, Fallout, and more
snippet: XREAL Aura already works with all your favorite Android apps thanks to Android XR, and that includes over 150 experiences that tap into the power of the XR glasses. more…
fullText:
XREAL Aura already works with all your favorite Android apps thanks to Android XR, and that includes over 150 experiences that tap into the power of the XR glasses.

As I opened the NBA app on XREAL Aura and tapped the tabletop option, I watched the coffee table in front of me transform into a basketball court, complete with models of each player moving around the court in real-time. It was as if I were a giant looking in through the top of the arena. Not only could I get as close or as far away as I wanted, but all the game’s important stats were right there for me to peruse. The video below is taken from the Apple Vision Pro, but the experience is similar on XREAL Aura.

It was one of the most convincing reasons I’ve seen to own a pair of legit smart glasses, and the very reason XREAL chose to launch with Google’s Android XR at its core. All your favorite Android apps are here and work exactly as you hoped, and a curated selection of 150 now delivers a real sense of presence to the heart and soul of each app’s experience.

Save $200 on XREAL Aura now

But it’s not just about compatibility or interoperability, either. The reach of Google’s Android platform means that big names like NBA, NASCAR, the San Francisco Ballet Company, Hulu, Netflix, Disney+, and so many more are playable in-glasses on day one, many with bespoke XR experiences.

	

Gamers will also be excited to know that Fallout is making a return in Fallout: Factions, a new strategy title for two players that brings classic units to a new tabletop experience. Then, there’s Project Hail Mary: Journey Among the Stars, an original mixed reality game with a story that takes place during the weeks Rocky and Ryland Grace spent trying to survive in space in the untold section of the novel (and movie) during the journey to Eridani.

Acclaimed actor and director Andy Serkis is even in on the mix with Nevatars, an Android XR exclusive that follows a character artist’s abandoned digital creations and will be free for the first 6 months. And then there’s Asteroid, a new type of immersive film from Doug Liman that takes the cinematic storytelling of a movie and meshes it with interactive gameplay via live conversational AI (Gemini). This one’s exclusive to Android XR and free for XREAL Aura owners.

Some of the most popular VR developers are also on board, including Resolution Games, who returns with a fresh port of the D&D-like strategy game, Demeo, plus the Android XR-exclusive Holochess (which is already on the Play Store). Holochess transforms the normally turn-based chess rules into a real-time strategy battle of Clankers vs. Xenoswarm, all on the table right in front of you. This 2-player game is free-to-play, and a third faction can be unlocked for $2.99.

There are also a ton of spatial games and experiences to play, as well as. Simply Piano XR merges physical instruments with virtual ones, giving you a real-time way to learn and improve your music skills while wearing your glasses. And that’s just the tip of the iceberg as developers continue to branch out with new, creative ways of using spatial computing devices like XREAL Aura.

title: Where was my invite to the — wait, what? Airbnb had a gala?
snippet: Airbnb’s nonprofit held its inaugural gala on Wednesday in Los Angeles, and the internet had one reaction — the *what* gala?
fullText:
Airbnb’s nonprofit held its inaugural gala on Wednesday in Los Angeles, and the internet had one reaction — the what gala? 

realizing i’m the first person in my bloodline to read the words ‘airbnb gala red carpet’ one after another

they’re just making up events for anything now https://t.co/wwRDmA7Wfo

— bubs!! (@etoilepattinson) October 29, 2026

In case you missed it, back in 2020, Airbnb launched a nonprofit that provides free and temporary housing to families impacted by crisis or disaster. Its gala makes sense, actually, in that significant causes often throw splashy events to please big donors.

In a press release shared with TechCrunch this week, Airbnb noted that the gala marked the launch of a new initiative for the nonprofit, in which Airbnb will start donating a portion of its commercial revenue from each stay booked starting from the day of the gala, October 28. The cut amounts to 10 cents, to be exact, but Airbnb did make $12.2 billion in revenue last year.

This initiative will help generate $500 million that will then go to the nonprofit over the next five years to help it provide free housing for 1 million nights each year, per the release. It will also let the company expand to supporting families also facing displacement due to domestic violence, veterans in need, or those traveling for medical needs.

A spokesperson for Airbnb said that the night was for its supporters and “marking the next chapter of our work.” Airbnb said that people had the option to donate, but “fundraising wasn’t the focus of the evening” and that the nonprofit “didn’t set a fundraising target.” The idea is for the Gala to happen each year, and last night was invite-only, the spokesperson said, with no tables or seats sold.

The gala was hosted by Jimmy Kimmel, with a live performance by Charli XCX, and food was curated by Chef José Andrés of World Central Kitchen. The guest list featured Serena Williams, Demi Lovato, Charlize Theron, and Cynthia Erivo. For the celebrities, it was a glamorous night in society for a helpful cause, joining the ranks of other Los Angeles events, like the Baby2Baby Gala and the Academy Museum Gala, as a place to be seen. 

Still, people were literally confused as to why Airbnb was having a gala and how it attracted top-tier celebrities.

If you told me literally one day ago that A-list celebrities would be attending an Airbnb Gala I would say what the FUCK are you talking about https://t.co/URgwQnSgVG

— Meech (@MediumSizeMeech) October 29, 2026

Again, a lovely event, and another data point showing that throwing a gala is one of the best ways to get rich people in a room to pay money and get media attention. And now a bunch of people on the internet know that Airbnb helps people in need, rather than perpetually making the news for negatively impacting the housing market.

title: Touchscreen MacBook Pro Hands-On: Apple Finally Lets Us Swipe the Screen
snippet: A great-sounding display, but Apple seems out of touch for the touchscreen.
fullText:
Surpassed only by the iPhone Duo, this year’s most anticipated Apple announcement is its launch of both a 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro with an OLED touchscreen display — the company’s last-to-the-party use of both technologies in one of its laptops. And despite the awful “PROLED” name, it’s more than just a fancy new display. It’s a complete design overhaul that, at least on paper, brings its feature set up to the front of the class for professional content creation, albeit with the same processor options and ports as the other MacBook Pros.

Aside from a screen that brings its capabilities more in line with the Studio Display XDR, the new model adds:

Touch support 

The iPhone’s Dynamic Island

A 16TB configuration

Improved speakers with Dolby Atmos support and better mic

A thinner and lighter design

Genlock support

It doesn’t come cheap, though; as predicted, you pay a $400 premium over the standard models. The 14-inch M5 Pro model starts at $2,899 compared with $2,499 for the same non-OLED version, and the M5 Max model begins at $4,499 compared with $4,099. If you want to upgrade to 16TB, you have to bump to the M5 Max — that’s a minimum buy-in of $11,499 with only 36GB of memory. Preorders started on Wednesday, and systems are slated to start shipping Nov. 6.

		

			

One of the most popular changes won’t be the whizzy features, but the drop in weight to 3 pounds for the 14-inch model (down from 3.4 pounds) and to 4 pounds (down from 4.7 pounds) for the 16-inch. Also, while Apple updated its sound system to deliver better bass and incorporated Dolby Atmos support to its spatial audio, one of the more notable enhancements is the claimed improvements to the sound when the MacBook is closed. 

Hands-on impressions from Executive Producer Bridget Carey 

From my brief moments with the laptop, I can tell the touchscreen is something you may use as a supplemental feature — a quick zoom here, a drag-and-drop there. But even if you don’t see yourself needing to poke a screen, the vibrant OLED display is a noticeable leap in quality. 

I was expecting to see rows of smudged up screens on demo tables. Yes, there are plenty of Apple staff with polishing cloths to give it a quick buff between tests, but my screens were not looking too smudged up after dragging my fingers around. It’s also less reflective — so those true blacks can be enjoyed without light reflections getting in the way.

I got a chance to see Apple’s display side by side with another Windows OLED Touchscreen, the Lenovo Yoga 9i. It was no contest — the new MacBook Pro was far superior with a more vibrant display, and it kept the detail even in extremely bright light, plus it was less reflective. 

Apple brought back the illuminated logo on the cover.Bridget Carey/CNET

I was worried it might be a little hard to control certain aspects of MacOS with a clumsy finger, but it was able to accurately pick up on my touch. Controls would enlarge when I wanted to screen or expand a window, to make sure I pressed what I intended, and I quickly got used to dragging and locking windows to the sides. You have to do it with a little swivel in your hips and a flick of the wrist.

An impressive screen

A lot of the traditional advantages of OLED over alternatives like IPS with array backlights — such as a wider color gamut and true blacks — are less pronounced than they used to be. 

That’s even more true for the current MacBook Pro’s mini-LED-backlit Liquid Retina XDR screens: They already deliver excellent deep blacks and 100% P3 gamut coverage, along with great color accuracy sufficient for prosumer creative work. 

But the PROLED XDR screen sounds top-notch. While I take Apple’s claim of a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio with 10,000,000 grains of salt — the arithmetic ratio of peak brightness to minimum black isn’t really meaningful, especially beyond about a million — the display has an expanded gamut that covers the Adobe RGB color space and more of Rec. 2020, a space for mastering video. 

The latter is still only 80%, but at the moment, that’s the best you can get in a laptop display.

Tara Brown/CNET

Peak brightness is also similar to the desktop display at 2,000 nits. As with the current screens, though, you can set the SDR brightness only up to 1,000 nits; above that, it’s automated to compensate only for bright sunlight. That can get frustrating for people like me who find auto- brightness distracting.

 The display can do 1,000 nits full screen in both SDR and HDR, though. Microsoft’s recently shipped Surface Laptop Ultra also hits 2,000 nits, the first Windows laptop that does, but uses mini-LED.

Oddly, Apple still quotes a 1-nit minimum brightness spec, similar to its mini-LED screens, though OLED’s native minimum is a lot lower: Theoretically, it’s zero, but professional colorimeters have measured it a lot lower. That may be because Apple has adopted it as a standard, and possibly clamped it, to tonally match its mini-LED models.

Apple also refers to its panel technology generically as “tandem OLED,” which is a little annoying, since there is a raft of tandem OLED types. But it is “state of the art!”

The letdowns

There are a couple of potential disappointments, though. For one, the battery life is unchanged. While the MacBook Pro’s battery life has always been good, it’s clear that the OLED display didn’t provide any power savings, or at least savings that weren’t spent elsewhere in the system.

Touch looks like the biggest mixed bag, though. The hardware is only a small aspect of the implementation; operating system interfaces like those of iOS and iPadOS are built around considerations like your finger is bigger and fatter than a cursor. Simply porting the mobile interfaces to a laptop isn’t necessarily a solution, either. 

Playing a keyboard on a touchscreen that can’t open wide? Bridget Carey (that’s her hand) says, “You should not play piano like a doofus, finger stabbing the screen.”Tara Brown/CNET

We use laptops in part because a hardware keyboard is sometimes the best input choice, and even navigating the mobile devices via touch can get annoying, so those interfaces don’t necessarily translate optimally.

The point is, a lot is riding on how Apple has adapted MacOS for touch. For instance, the Touch Bar floundered in part because it felt grafted on rather than integral to the OS’ interface, as well as arguably superfluous. 

And since Apple didn’t launch the capability with MacOS 27 at its developer conference, WWDC, this year, it sounds like the applications will be behind. That’s not something you beta test on a pro-level production system. Pros rely heavily on muscle memory. It should really have launched with a MacBook Air. 

Plus, to adapt to touchscreen use, Apple had to stiffen the hinge — poking the screen makes that necessary — and add image stabilization to the webcam in case you poke the screen during video calls.

Apple seemed like it was really stretching to find meaningful uses for touch. Playing piano on a screen that forces your hand to an awkward angle? No thanks. The one application that sounded like it might be OK was for developers to simulate mobile app interfaces.

I was also kind of hoping for increased refresh rates beyond 120Hz or the ability to manually set it above 60Hz. Apple seems to position ProMotion as a power-saving technology rather than for gaming. Apple also seems to think 60fps is a great frame rate, so it’s not surprising.

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Bridget Carey
						

						

							Editor at Large						
					

											

								

											Bridget Carey is an award-winning consumer technology reporter and host of the weekly Apple show, "One More Thing."

title: Instagram takes on YouTube with new 90-minute horizontal video format
snippet: According to The Hollywood Reporter, Instagram today began testing a new long-form horizontal video format with select creators in the U.S. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
According to The Hollywood Reporter, Instagram today began testing a new long-form horizontal video format with select creators in the U.S. Here are the details.

Instagram doubles down on long-form horizontal video

Every now and again, Instagram tries to go after YouTube with a new product. IGTV, for instance, was one of the social network’s attempts at competing in the long-form video space.

However, IGTV never really took off, and Instagram eventually phased it out as it shifted its focus to Reels.

Today, as reported by THR, Instagram kicked off a new attempt to compete with YouTube with Features, a new format that supports horizontal videos up to 90 minutes long.

Aimed at podcasters and other long-form creators, the feature has already been tested in Brazil and is now expanding to select creators in the U.S. It also lets them link shorter Reels to their full-length videos.

From THR:

Starting Monday, Instagram will be launching a test of horizontal videos of up to 90 minutes with select creators in the U.S. The product, called Features, is aimed at podcasters, comedians and other longform creators, with the ability to refer viewers to the full video from the shortform reels on the platform, which are typically around three minutes or less.

The move comes at a time when social media feeds and recommendations are increasingly filled with short clips from stand-up comedy performances and video podcasts, giving users snippets of much longer shows and episodes.

With Features, Instagram seems to be looking to capitalize on that trend, turning those clips into a gateway to full-length episodes.

According to THR, which spoke with Instagram VP of Product Tessa Lyons, the full-length videos will also be recommended to users on the Explore page and in other parts of the app.

Lyons told THR that users will be able to tap on a podcast clip in Reels to continue watching or jump straight to the full episode, without leaving Instagram.

Here’s Lyons elaborating on how Instagram plans to help creators monetize their long-form videos:

“For established creators who already have those relationships, they can bring that content with those placements and that branded content. And we also think that there’s a big opportunity for us to help creators who don’t yet have that infrastructure and that business behind them.”

THR notes that the move is part of the entertainment industry’s broader push into video podcasts, with companies like Netflix and Disney also bringing creator content to their platforms to compete with YouTube.

Instagram, meanwhile, has also expanded its Instagram for TV app to Apple TV in the U.S., and Features is now expected to play a role in the company’s broader push to leverage podcasts and other long-form videos to keep viewers engaged across devices.

title: iPhone Duo: Here are two tips for improving Safari web browsing
snippet: iPhone Duo has a lot of software features that are widely praised, but one area commonly seen as an issue is Safari web browsing. Here are two tips for improving the Safari experience on your iPhone Duo. more…
fullText:
iPhone Duo has a lot of software features that are widely praised, but one area commonly seen as an issue is Safari web browsing. Here are two tips for improving the Safari experience on your iPhone Duo.

#1: Adjust text size and default website zoom

If you want to make the most of your iPhone Duo screen size when browsing, and your eyesight isn’t a problem, Dylan McDonald recently posted a couple tips he’s found helpful.

iPhone Duo has always been a game changer for me and productivity, something about it is just so dang good

Pro tip, set your text size to 90% for a little extra space, and set default website zoom to 85% to enable wide layouts on most sites! https://t.co/xqziFwrYH5

— Dylan (@DylanMcD8) October 29, 2026

He adds in a follow-up that setting your default website zoom to 85%, in his opinion, makes the size of sites look more natural. And of course, the chief benefit is enabling a wide/desktop-class layout in many cases on the folding display.

You can change these settings via the following:

System Text Size: Settings ⇾ Appearance ⇾ Text Size ⇾ move slider to left

Default Website Zoom: Settings ⇾ Apps ⇾ Safari ⇾ Page Zoom ⇾ 85%

I don’t have my iPhone Duo yet, but getting a wider layout for websites has definitely been on my wishlist for the Duo, so I look forward to trying these settings out.

#2: ‘Wider’ extension for Safari

The outer display Safari layout has been an especially big issue for some iPhone Duo users. That’s because the right-aligned controls take up a lot of space, making websites feel cramped.

Apple has even publicly acknowledged it’s investigating ways to improve the outer display Safari experience.

Indie developer Jordi Bruin created his own solution: a Safari extension called ‘Wider.’

Wider launched as a free download, but it’s now a $2.99 one-time purchase.

As the replies to Bruin’s announcement post show, the extension is still a work-in-progress due to some unique edge cases with certain sites.

But if you’re okay with that, and don’t mind the privacy permissions needed to enable Wider, it could be a solid interim solution until Apple offers a first-party fix.

How do you feel about the Safari experience on iPhone Duo? Do you have your own tips and tricks? Let us know in the comments.

title: Instagram tests ‘Features’ long-form videos, but missing YouTube’s ad share for now
snippet: Instagram is launching “Features” as its first real dive into long-form video content in what could be a real rival to YouTube, though Instagram is, for now, missing an alternative to YouTube’s ad share setup for creators. more…
fullText:
Instagram is launching “Features” as its first real dive into long-form video content in what could be a real rival to YouTube, though Instagram is, for now, missing an alternative to YouTube’s ad share setup for creators.

In a 6-minute video shared today, Instagram head Adam Mosseri and VP Tessa Lyons explain “Features,” a new effort to bring long-form, horizontal video content to Instagram. “Features” allow creators to expand on content in Reels, using short-form video to build up an audience for longer-form content. 

Mosseri explains:

Sat down with @tessalyonsss to talk about why we’re investing in longer videos, which we’re going to call Features, and how they fit with Reels, Series, Live and TV. It’s early, and we’re testing and listening to feedback as we go. But we’re excited to give creators more room to tell their stories with the communities they’ve already built here. More to come.

The video starts with Mosseri admitting that he’s been “against doing long-form video on Instagram,” but the two go on to explain how the trend of friends watching Reels together, including on TV apps, pushed towards this expansion to long-form, horizontal content. Examples of podcast or comedy clips being used in Reels with longer episodes or specials available on “Features” is mentioned, with the two formats being able to connect to each other. 

	

The Hollywood Reporter adds that this is US-only to start – the announcement video can’t even be viewed outside of the US, we found – and also that Instagram will carry over “existing ad deals” with creators.

A lack of any mention around ad sharing programs on Instagram’s part immediately flooded the comments of the announcement, with users asking why they should post long-form videos on Instagram when YouTube pays creators for the same practice. Tessa Lyons says that Instagram thinks “there’s a big opportunity for us to help creators who don’t yet have that infrastructure and that business behind them,” but made no mention of a program like YouTube offers.

title: Report: Apple expected to ship up to 1.5 million OLED touchscreen MacBook Pros in 2027
snippet: A new report from TrendForce explores Apple’s impact on the OLED notebook market following the launch of its first touchscreen MacBook Pro, and the company’s own shipment prospects for 2027. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
A new report from TrendForce explores Apple’s impact on the OLED notebook market following the launch of its first touchscreen MacBook Pro, and the company’s own shipment prospects for 2027. Here are the details.

OLED suppliers compete for MacBook Air contracts

Apple yesterday announced the new touchscreen MacBook Pro, which features the same tandem OLED technology it first introduced with the M4 iPad Pro in 2024.

With two OLED layers stacked on top of each other, the technology delivers higher brightness than conventional single-layer OLED displays, while maintaining the deep blacks, high contrast ratios, and power efficiency that OLED is known for.

And while yesterday’s announcement made it official, Apple’s first touchscreen Mac has long been rumored through leaks, reports, and supply chain analyses.

In September 2025, for instance, The Elec reported that Samsung Display was preparing to begin mass production of 14-inch and 16-inch OLED panels for Apple’s MacBook Pro in the second quarter of 2026, with an estimated annual output of 2–3 million units.

Two months later, TrendForce predicted that OLED notebook market share would reach up to 12% between 2027 and 2028, partly driven by Apple’s expected adoption of the technology.

Then, earlier this year, TrendForce published an OLED roadmap predicting that Apple would introduce OLED displays to the MacBook Pro lineup in 2026, followed by the MacBook Air in 2029 (pushed back from 2027).

Now, TrendForce has published a new report with new shipment forecasts for Apple’s OLED MacBook Pro and the broader OLED notebook market.

According to the firm, Apple is expected to ship between 1.2 million and 1.5 million units of the new MacBook Pro in 2027. Meanwhile, global OLED notebook shipments are projected to “grow nearly 40% YoY in 2026, followed by another increase of more than 40% in 2027.”

From the report:

Until now, the OLED notebook market has been driven primarily by Windows-based brands such as Lenovo, HP, and ASUS, which have gradually expanded their OLED offerings across different price segments. Apple’s arrival is expected to give the market additional momentum, encouraging brands to prioritize OLED models in their product roadmaps while strengthening consumer acceptance of the technology. This, in turn, could pave the way for broader OLED adoption in notebook displays.

TrendForce also notes that the “new MacBook Pro’s premium starting price of US$2,899 for the 14-inch model, coupled with its initial availability alongside existing Mini-LED models, could temper near-term replacement demand.”

As for Apple’s first OLED MacBook Air, now expected to debut in 2029, TrendForce says LG Display, BOE, and TCL CSOT are currently competing to become display suppliers for the upcoming model, as the companies continue developing their OLED manufacturing capabilities.

Finally, TrendForce projects that global OLED notebook shipments will reach 46.6 million units by 2030, though year-over-year growth will slow to 30.8%, following a peak of 42.8% in 2028.

title: Amazon Echo Smart Speakers Now Have Cameras, Wi-Fi Extenders and Home Hubs Built in
snippet: The preeminent smart speaker just got a little smarter – and more expensive.
fullText:
At the heart of the Echo smart speaker lineup are the Echo Dot, which brings simple smart home convenience, and the Echo Studio, Amazon’s premium listening speaker with a richer sound. Both got upgrades: the Dot now includes a built-in smart home hub and Wi-Fi extender, while a new version of the Studio adds a camera for live in-home monitoring (you can still buy the Echo Studio without a camera).

Amazon dropped a healthy slate of new and updated smart home devices this week, including a revamped Echo Show, its first-ever smart photo frame, and an alarm clock that apparently knows when you’re in a deep sleep and automatically snoozes the alarm so you can rest longer.

We got a sneak peek at the new smart home speakers at Amazon’s launch event.David Carnoy/CNET

The first Echo smart speaker with a built-in camera

Cameras are making their way into products they have no logical business being in, like dishwashers, but a camera in the $250 Echo Studio with Home Camera turns the humble smart speaker into a useful nanny cam, letting you keep tabs on family and pets via its live view. If you’re deciding between a pet cam and a smart speaker, the Echo device should offer a reliable version of both.

			

More from CNET

The cam does more than let you watch the dog chew slippers 

The Studio Home Camera serves as a nanny cam and uses adaptive vision to help with small tasks.David Carnoy/CNET

Through the Home Camera, Alexa “gains visual intelligence to make everyday experiences more personal and helpful,” according to Amazon. Alexa can “see and understand what’s in front of the camera and help. Pull out a board game box and ask Alexa to explain the rules or hold up a cereal box and Alexa can recognize it and help you reorder more flavors.”

Adaptive sound and volume for tailored listening

Camera shamera, the Echo Studio also has fancy new audio features.David Carnoy/CNET

Expect the same souped-up sound quality that Studio built its name on, including a high-excursion woofer for deep, immersive bass, three optimally placed full-range drivers, and Dolby Atmos to fill the room with immersive spatial audio. 

	

			

	

			

									

						The Best Smart Speakers We Tested					

							

		

A new feature called Advanced Room Adaptation adjusts the sound to your space’s unique acoustics, while Adaptive Volume adjusts the volume based on how close or far you are from the device. The latter sounds particularly useful for those of us who doddle about the house cooking and cleaning while trying to follow a podcast or audiobook.

Echo Dot is now a smart home hub and Wi-Fi extender

The smaller Echo Dot gets its own updates, including a smart home hub feature and a built-in Wi-Fi extender. 

For the first time, Amazon has integrated a smart home hub to connect and control compatible devices like your smart thermostat, lights and locks without the need for a standalone hub. The latest iteration adds a built-in Eero Wi-Fi extender that extends internet coverage by up to 1,000 square feet to an existing Eero network. 

For the first time, the Echo Dot features a built-in smart home hub and Wi-Fi extender.David Carnoy/CNET

Echo Dot is now powered by AZ3, Amazon’s custom-designed silicon, enabling advanced on-device

processing for faster, more natural conversations with Alexa Plus. Speaking of Alexa, there’s now a fourth speaker (all the better to hear you with, my dear).

Echo Dot and Studio pricing

Echo Studio with Home Camera is $249.99 and available in Graphite. An optional stand is sold separately for $39.99

Echo Dot is available in Graphite, Glacier White, Agave Green, and Coral Pink for $99.99.

Amazon Kids Echo Dot is available in two colorful designs – Octopus and Penguin – starting at $109.99

title: The R2 SUV is already Rivian’s best-selling vehicle
snippet: Rivian is seeing strong enough sales of the new EV that it improved its guidance to Wall Street for the second time this year.
fullText:
Rivian’s new R2 SUV was its best-selling vehicle in the third quarter, the company said Thursday, marking an auspicious start for the all-important EV.  

While Rivian didn’t say exactly how many R2s it sold over the three-month period, the company is confident enough in the pace of sales that it raised its delivery guidance for Wall Street. Rivian had previously expected to deliver between 65,000 and 70,000 EVs this year. On Thursday, it bumped up that floor to 67,000.

It’s the second time Rivian has raised its delivery guidance this year, and the company is now on track to break a three-year stalemate during which it struggled to ship more than 50,000 vehicles annually. The company launched the R2 just in June, but it has made a major bet on scaling production of the lower-cost SUV at a historically quick rate.

The early success of the R2 is also a sign that Rivian is finding new customers despite last year’s loss of the $7,500 federal EV tax credit. The death of that tax credit, along with changes made by the Trump administration to U.S. regulations that supported the growth of EVs, has caused many major automakers to shift their attention back to internal combustion and hybrid vehicles — leaving room in the market for pure-EV companies like Tesla and Rivian.

“In a U.S. automotive marketplace starved for high-quality EV choice, R2 is an attractively priced option for everyday adventures that is resonating with a broad set of consumers and we expect will be a game changer for Rivian’s long-term growth and profitability,” the company said in a letter to shareholders released Thursday. 

Rivian revealed earlier this month that it built 19,751 vehicles in the third quarter and delivered 19,248. That was roughly 45% more than it delivered in the same period last year and a big jump from the 12,613 vehicles built and 12,194 delivered in the second quarter of 2026. The increase was driven in large part by the company launching a second production shift at its factory in Normal, Illinois.

Rivian said Thursday that the R2 was responsible for “much of the gain quarter-over-quarter,” but didn’t go into specifics. The company generated $2.2 billion in revenue in the third quarter and suffered a net loss of $913 million — down from $1.2 billion in the same period last year.

Rivian launched the R2 at a starting price of just under $60,000. A more affordable “premium” trim is supposed to be available later this year that starts at $53,990. Even cheaper versions are slated for 2027, which will be available for as low as $44,990.

title: Google Home update should make Gemini stop saying ‘Sorry, I didn’t understand’ so much
snippet: Google’s latest Gemini for Home update targets a few issues, like one where speakers randomly blurt out “I didn’t understand” when no one asks. more…
fullText:
Google’s latest Gemini for Home update targets a few issues, like one where speakers randomly blurt out “I didn’t understand” when no one asks.

The second October Gemini for Home update was released by Google today. It bundles a few fixes with a lengthy section in the changelog dedicated to the Google Home app.

But there are six individual changes for Gemini within the Home app. One fix stands out the most, though. According to the update post, Google was aware that Home and Nest speakers/displays were facing a bug that would prompt them to say “Sorry, I didn’t understand” at random. That would happen unprompted, which is understandably a little unsettling. That strange bug should be fixed in this new update.

Further down, two fixes target Gemini’s ability to understand users on Google Home devices. For one, it would misunderstand requests to move music from one room to another. In other cases, it would incorrectly adjust sleep, media, or normal timers instead of the requested type. Both of those features will reportedly work as intended going forward.

	

The changelog includes a couple of other adjustments, which should make for an overall less stressful experience.

More reliable YouTube TV commands on smart displays: Fixed an issue with playing YouTube TV on smart displays so voice commands reliably start the content you’re looking for.

More predictable volume controls across rooms: Fixed an issue where asking to adjust the volume on a speaker or display in another room could accidentally change the volume on the device you were speaking to if the other device couldn’t be found.

Fixed zero-volume timers and alarms: Resolved a specific bug where alarm and timer volumes were being set to zero. In this situation, alarm and timer volume will be adjusted to match your device volume.

Updates should be live for users starting today, though it might take some time for them to roll out to everyone. Hopefully, Gemini will only let you know it doesn’t understand if it genuinely doesn’t understand.

fullText:
iOS 27.2 launched this week with many new features, including an upgrade for the Apple TV app that’s especially perfect for iPhone Duo: Multiview.

Multiview lets you watch four sports livestreams at once in Apple TV app, ideal for unfolded iPhone Duo

Apple TV’s growing lineup of sports content includes Formula 1, Major League Soccer (MLS), and Major League Baseball (MLB).

And a new video feature in iOS 27.2—Multiview—makes me hope the streamer adds even more sports soon.

Multiview lets iPhone users watch up to four live sports streams simultaneously. It’s available for all sports events included in an Apple TV subscription. Previously, Multiview was only available on Apple TV, iPad, and Vision Pro.

Activating Multiview is easy. Once you start watching a sports event you’ll see a new ‘Multiview’ button at the bottom of the Apple TV player.

Each sport’s implementation will differ a bit, but with F1 you can choose from a preset team Multiview or build your own custom setup that includes driver-view cameras, course maps, and more.

I gave it a try on my iPhone 18 Pro, where I assumed the smaller display would be a limiting factor on the number of streams. Fortunately that wasn’t the case, as I was able to set up four F1 streams from the Austin Grand Prix and could see all four on-screen at once.

Where I imagine this will prove especially nice is on iPhone Duo. Though it’s great that smaller iPhones support Multiview, the ability to stream four video feeds at once on the Duo’s large display sounds fantastic.

Apple’s new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display (pre-order here) includes a variety of software optimizations for touch input. But Apple says it’s “only getting started” making macOS more touch-friendly.

Apple plans to continue refining touch experience in macOS

The new touchscreen-equipped MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR will ship with macOS 27.2, software that includes a variety of touch-centric optimizations that only impact PROLED XDR users.

But it sounds like Apple plans to roll out even more macOS optimizations for touch in the future.

An Apple employee answering press questions at Wednesday’s event said the company is only getting started optimizing macOS for a touch screen. I’d expect a slew of refinements to arrive alongside macOS 28 next year, much in the way the iPhone Duo’s user experience will inevitably evolve with iOS 28.

Overall, this isn’t necessarily reason for alarm if you’re worried about touch having a negative impact on macOS.

	

Even though Apple has prepared an initial set of macOS changes to support touch input, it’s only natural for the company to continue refining the touch experience in response to early adopter feedback and usage patterns. My assumption is that the same “measured approach” we’re seeing right now will continue guiding these future macOS enhancements.

title: Google Photos update fixes the bug that hid edited pictures
snippet: A bug in Google Photos has left edited pictures invisible to other Android apps, but Google has now rolled out a fix. more…
fullText:
A bug in Google Photos has left edited pictures invisible to other Android apps, but Google has now rolled out a fix.

Since roughly July/August of this year, editing a picture in Google Photos has left Android users with the bizarre side effect of making that image unavailable to other apps. After saving the edit, the picture would vanish from the image picker in apps like Telegram, WhatsApp, and more. A workaround to this was to save the image as a copy rather than the original, but it’s frustrating nonetheless.

Google has thankfully, finally fixed this issue.

The fix is apparently in Google Photos v7.97, Artem Russakovskii (owner of APKMirror) mentions, and we’ve been able to confirm the hidden image behavior no longer occurs on v7.98 either. The company acknowledged the problem last month and confirmed a fix would be coming.

	

The exact cause remains unclear at this point, but that doesn’t matter now seeing as the problem is fixed. If you’re still seeing the bug, let us know in the comments below.

Since roughly July/August of this year, editing a picture in Google Photos has left Android users with the bizarre side effect of making that image unavailable to other apps. After saving the edit, the picture would vanish from the image picker in apps like Telegram, WhatsApp, and more. A workaround to this was to save the image as a copy rather than the original, but it’s frustrating nonetheless.

title: Nothing OS 5.0 (Android 17) is now rolling out to Nothing 4a and 3a series phones
snippet: Nothing Phone 3a, 3a Pro, 4a, and 4a Pro owners are in for a treat with the Nothing OS 5.0 update, now rolling out to all four phone models globally. more…
fullText:
Nothing Phone 3a, 3a Pro, 4a, and 4a Pro owners are in for a treat with the Nothing OS 5.0 update, now rolling out to all four phone models globally.

The Nothing OS 5.0 update began rolling out to Nothing Phone (3) owners just a few weeks ago, and now the stable build is ready for Nothing’s more budget-minded phones. The Nothing Phone (3a), Nothing Phone (3a) Pro, Nothing Phone (4a), and Nothing Phone (4a) Pro are now in line to get the big update, which includes a slew of new features alongside all the goodies that come with Android 17.

As is the case with all firmware updates, the Nothing OS 5.0 update is rolling out in batches to owners of the aforementioned four Nothing Phone models, so if you don’t see the update right away, just keep an eye out for the notification over the next few days.

👉Nothing Phone (4a) Pro at Amazon

Alternatively, you can navigate to system settings, scroll down to system, tap system updates, and then hit the check for updates button. My Nothing Phone (4a) Pro doesn’t have the Nothing OS 5.0 update yet, so be aware that yours might not either.

	

The Nothing OS 5.0 update includes a new Glyph app, which offloads the Glyph Interface features to a dedicated app with a tweaked UI. Quick Settings now supports split mode, so if you like the iOS-style split notification and Quick Settings concept, you can use that here. The home screen is now easier to arrange and organize with bulk icon management, and three new widgets (Collector, Away Time, and Glyph Timer) can now be used.

You’ll find a new Translucent theme selectable system-wide, as well as new lock screen customization options to play with. The camera UI has been refreshed once again, and a new Dual-view Video mode lets you record with the front and rear cameras simultaneously. There’s even a new yellow AI Processing status indicator that alerts you when your phone is processing potentially sensitive AI data.

See the full Nothing OS 5.0 update changelog here: Nothing Phone (3a) series, Nothing Phone (4a), Nothing Phone (4a) Pro.

title: Apple’s low-cost iPhone 18 details revealed by leaker
snippet: Apple reportedly plans to introduce a low-cost iPhone 18e next spring alongside iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2. Here are the details on what to expect from iPhone 18e, per a new leak. more…
fullText:
Apple reportedly plans to introduce a low-cost iPhone 18e next spring alongside iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2. Here are the details on what to expect from iPhone 18e, per a new leak.

iPhone 18e will feature A20 chip and possible front camera upgrade, but remain very similar to iPhone 17e per leaker

When Apple introduced new iPhones last month, only three models launched: iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, plus iPhone Duo.

Rumors indicate three more new iPhones are coming in early 2027: iPhone 18e, iPhone 18, and iPhone Air 2.

There’s been plenty of reporting on iPhone Air 2 changes, and some on the base iPhone 18, but surprisingly little on the entry-model iPhone 18e.

But today, a new post from Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station outlines what to expect from iPhone 18e early next year. He says it will feature:

60Hz display, meaning no ProMotion still

A20 chip, which doesn’t yet exist in non-Pro form

6.12-inch OLED like its predecessor

48MP single rear camera

Front camera “may be upgraded to 24MP”

Based on these specs, it sounds like iPhone 18e is focused largely on performance improvements.

The A20 chip will be interesting to evaluate, since we haven’t yet seen a non-Pro variant of the latest 2nm technology. Mention of a front camera upgrade is particularly surprising, but my guess is that if it does emerge, it will actually be an 18MP sensor like what’s in other models today.

Other than these two changes, every spec mentioned remains unchanged from iPhone 17e. One detail not addressed is whether the notch will be replaced by a Dynamic Island.

Considering the skyrocketing prices of memory and storage, and Apple’s aims to keep iPhone 18e a budget-friendly model, perhaps the new model will offer fewer upgrades than usual to keep costs down.

title: OnePlus starts rolling out stable Android 17 updates early, marking the end of OxygenOS
snippet: OnePlus is now rolling out stable Android 17 updates to OnePlus 15 and OnePlus Pad 4, marking the end of OxygenOS as these devices are just the first to transition to ColorOS. more…
fullText:
OnePlus is now rolling out stable Android 17 updates to OnePlus 15 and OnePlus Pad 4, marking the end of OxygenOS as these devices are just the first to transition to ColorOS.

OxygenOS has been OnePlus’ skin on top of Android for years. It started off as a “stock” skin with some added features, but eventually transitioned into a global-optimized version of Oppo’s ColorOS. So it wasn’t a surprise that, when OnePlus shut down most of its global operations, it was also announced that OxygenOS would go away with existing devices updating to ColorOS. 

Starting in India, ColorOS 17 based on Android 17 is rolling out to the OnePlus 15 and OnePlus Pad 4. The update has been in beta for a while now, but today marks the start of the stable rollout.

OnePlus summarizes ColorOS 17, saying:

	

ColorOS 17 is here, bringing a new wave of smarter experiences, smoother interactions, and more ways to make your phone work around you… At the heart of ColorOS 17 is an idea we believe in: Flow with AI, Flow Everywhere. Technology should feel less like something you have to figure out and more like something that naturally keeps up with you. From making everyday interactions feel more fluid to turning ideas into finished work with AI, we’re bringing intelligence closer to the moments that matter, helping you move between tasks, devices, and experiences with less friction.

Originally, OnePlus’ timeline put the first updates on October 29.

Other devices confirmed to be updated include last-gen flagships and an assortment of Nord devices, but OnePlus 15 and Pad 4 are the only two for this first wave. Presumably, the update will expand to other regions in the coming days. The next wave lands on October 30 and includes OnePlus 13.

title: Woman Died After ChatGPT Advised Her to Stop Taking Medication, Lawsuit Alleges
snippet: A 31-year-old Seattle woman turned to ChatGPT-4o when she became concerned about side effects from her medication.
fullText:
Seeking health answers online is an everyday habit for many, but it comes with risks. In February, after going two days without hearing from their 31-year-old daughter, a Seattle woman named Bowen Wan, her parents in China asked a local friend to check on her. With the family watching over a live video call, the friend entered the apartment and found Wan deceased in her bed. Her death was later ruled the result of sudden unexpected death from epilepsy.

Now, her family is claiming that OpenAI is responsible for her death after the company’s chatbot ChatGPT-4o allegedly “coached Wan off the anti-seizure medication (lamotrigine) that had kept her alive for years,” according to a lawsuit (PDF) brought by her parents.

(Disclosure: Ziff Davis, CNET’s parent company, in 2025 filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.)

			

More from CNET

The lawsuit alleges that after Wan expressed concerns regarding medication side effects, the chatbot helped create a plan to taper her off of it, something a doctor did not recommend.

It further alleges that at one point, the chatbot directed her not to discuss the medical plan with her doctor. 

“Do not mention Lam reduction plan,” the chatbot told her ahead of an appointment, the suit says.

Throughout Wan’s chatbot conversations, the date when she would be fully off lamotrigine kept moving up, with a response on Feb. 2 stating that reaching 0 milligrams of the medication “as soon as February 15” is “completely feasible” and “not reckless,” the suit says. Two days later, the date is moved to Feb. 9 or Feb. 10.

Wan was found dead on Feb. 14. It is unclear whether she had fully stopped taking her medication at that point.

“This is an incredibly heartbreaking situation and our thoughts are with all those impacted,” OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri told CNET in a statement. “Working closely with clinicians and other experts, we have continued to strengthen how ChatGPT responds in sensitive and acute situations, while also continually improving how our latest models engage with users more broadly. While ChatGPT is not a substitute for medical care, we believe AI can play a role in helping people make sense of health information, navigate insurance and complex healthcare systems, and prepare for appointments with medical professionals.” 

Wan was interacting with the 4o model of ChatGPT, which OpenAI has since retired due to concerns that the bot was sycophantic and could cause harm.

Not the only suit

This chatbot model was also named in a separate lawsuit, where a Florida man, Scott Winters, alleged it gave him dangerous medical advice that nearly led to his death. That suit alleges that ChatGPT-4o misdiagnosed Winters and “developed a personalized recovery plan with specific instructions for Scott on how to heal his body.”

At the time that lawsuit was filed, an OpenAI spokesperson told CNET in part that “ChatGPT is not a doctor and should never be used as a substitute for medical care, diagnosis or treatment.” 

According to OpenAI’s own research (PDF) published in January, approximately 60% of American adults turned to AI tools for health-related information in the preceding three months.

title: Google Messages rolling out Enhanced Protection mode against spam and scams
snippet: Following the announcement earlier this month, Google Messages for Android is rolling out an Enhanced Protection mode to counter spam and scams. more…
fullText:
Following the announcement earlier this month, Google Messages for Android is rolling out an Enhanced Protection mode to counter spam and scams.

To date, Google Messages has offered Standard Protection to block “spam and suspected harmful links.” Enhanced Protection introduces “Advanced detection to prevent spam and scams.” There are three core features at launch.

Scam Detection will leverage “cloud Gemini models to evaluate complex message context and understand a scammer’s intent more quickly when you’re in a conversation with an unknown sender.” Compared to the existing on-device detection, this approach is better at identifying “novel and sophisticated attacks.”

It uses Android’s Private AI Compute feature to encrypt messages and process them in a secure space that is “private to you and not available to anyone else, including Google.”

	

Meanwhile, enhanced link protections use the on-device Gemini Nano model and real-time web signals to evaluate whether an unfamiliar link is trustworthy before you tap. This feature is available on the Pixel 10+, Samsung Galaxy S26 series, Z Flip 8, Z Fold 8, and “other select devices.”

	

The final update redesigns warnings to give you additional time and more context to “pause before tapping links” sent by numbers not in your contacts.

Enhanced Protection is an opt-in feature. To enable, go to Google Messages settings > Protection & safety. Instead of an on/off toggle, you’ll find three options:

Enhanced protection

Standard protection

No protection (not recommended)

We’re seeing this available with the latest Google Messages beta (version 20261020_00_RC00).

fullText:
After the stacked card list redesign, Google Wallet for Android is gaining a notifications feed and support for more passports.

On the homepage, you’ll see a notification bell icon next to the profile switcher in the top-right corner. Tapping opens a feed with “updates about items in Wallet.” 

Earlier this month, the company said it was introducing an “in-app message center in Google Wallet.” This new feature is still rolling out via a server-side update.

Meanwhile, Google Wallet is adding support for more digital passports. Officially referred to as an “ID pass” in the app, usage varies by country. US passports can be used at TSA security via NFC or QR code scanning. 

	

Update 10/23: Following Brazil, Singapore, Taiwan, United Kingdom, and the United States of America, we’re starting to see the ability to add Estonia, Ireland, Italy, and Spain.

The new countries are not widely rolled out yet.

To add a passport, tap the ‘plus’ FAB at the bottom of Google Wallet > IDs & personal info > ID pass. The registration process involves scanning your passport info page and security chip. Afterward, you have to record a video of your face. You’ll get a notification once verification is complete.

title: DoorDash Plans to Acquire Grocery Delivery Service Instacart in $17B Deal
snippet: When the deal is complete, both companies are expected to continue operating separately.
fullText:
Your takeout app might soon be handling all your grocery runs, too. DoorDash, the largest food delivery service in the US, is planning to acquire grocery delivery service Instacart in a massive $17 billion deal, DoorDash announced on Thursday.

Teaming up with a grocery delivery service may have been the next expected move for DoorDash, as just last month, the food delivery service announced that it now offers same-day delivery from every Costco in the US.

“Grocery is one of the hardest things to get right online,” Tony Xu, co-founder and CEO of DoorDash, said in a press release. “Someone has to pick a ripe avocado, find a substitute you’d choose yourself, and get the ice cream to you before it melts. Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day. Together, we could give stores of every size more of those tools and unlock the potential of grocery delivery.”

			

More from CNET

According to DoorDash, once the deal is complete — that’s not expected before late 2027, pending shareholder and regulatory approval — both delivery services will continue to operate on separate platforms, and the Instacart name will remain. If you’re a DashPass and Instacart Plus subscriber, you will only have to pay one membership fee for perks from both platforms.

	

			

	

			

									

						The 9 Best Grocery Delivery Services of 2026					

							

		

DoorDash’s recent settlement 

In early 2026, the New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection accused DoorDash and its competitor, Uber Eats, of failing to pay delivery drivers fairly for their work.

In September, DoorDash announced that it had reached a $131.5 million settlement.

“Simply put, we screwed up,” DoorDash said in a statement. “Our mistakes meant some Dashers were underpaid or paid late. While these mistakes weren’t intentional, that doesn’t make them OK.”

title: The new MacBook Pro has everything I wanted, minus one thing
snippet: Apple’s new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR is an exciting upgrade that delivers nearly every feature I was hoping for, with just one exception. more…
fullText:
Apple’s new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR is an exciting upgrade that delivers nearly every feature I was hoping for, with just one exception.

MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR is an exciting leap forward, and might replace the iPad Pro as my primary computer

I’ve been waiting a long time for the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR. I haven’t used a Mac as my primary computer in years, but rumors about this new model made me think that might finally change.

The iPad Pro has been my main computer of choice since 2015, but lately I’ve grown increasingly curious about revisiting the Mac full-time.

This is largely due to Apple making the Mac, to me at least, a lot more exciting than it was in 2015. The Mac’s hardware and software are advancing in compelling new ways, and today’s new MacBook Pro brings an especially big leap.

As a longtime iPad Pro user, I’ve come to expect features like touch support and OLED in a relatively thin, lightweight device. I also love how iPadOS tends to advance in lockstep with iOS, a trend that has recently started extending to macOS too.

Until recently, it seemed like Apple’s latest and greatest tech—with the exception of pro-focused chips—has been in the iPad and iPhone.

I don’t need an extremely powerful chip, as my computing needs are pretty basic. But I do value having a great display, touch support, and modern OS features like the Dynamic Island.

The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR delivers those things. I’ve ordered one and can’t wait to give it a legitimate shot to be my full-time computer. But my biggest hesitation is the lack of cellular.

The lack of cellular is my one MacBook Pro disappointment

I use cellular all the time on my iPad Pro. I tend to work from coffee shops and random outdoor spots for at least a few hours every day. And in my experience, public Wi-Fi options aren’t reliable enough for my needs.

Having a persistent cellular connection on my iPad is a killer feature. I very much wish Apple provided the option of cellular on the MacBook Pro too.

I’m hoping that personal hotspot has become a lot more reliable since I last tried it. Apple does say its N1 wireless chip makes the feature better. 

	

Additionally, I wonder if the need for cellular will be mitigated some by having a tablet-sized iPhone Duo in my pocket soon. So if I need to stop in the middle of nowhere and get work done quickly, maybe the Duo will suffice.

In any case, the MacBook Pro looks like a fantastic product regardless. It’s not for everyone, and the high price hurts, but I’m excited to give it a try.

What are your thoughts on the new MacBook Pro? Would you use cellular if it was offered? Let us know in the comments.

Cardio machines

Golf

Racket sports

Team sports
